strategy: blight persist-recursion control / counters as spent persists
identity: A W/B control deck that answers the board with eight maindeck interaction cards at MV 1-6 — six of them cheap removal at MV 1-3 — and then wins because its own creatures stop staying dead. It is stated as removal-plus-recursion rather than as a persist deck, because the persist blanket is one card of forty: Isilu, Carrier of Twilight — the back face of Eirdu — grants every other nontoken creature persist, and it is the ceiling, not the floor. The floor is that Reaping Willow, Dose of Dawnglow, Graveshifter and Retched Wretch all rebuy creatures with no reference to Isilu at all. What makes the blight mechanic matter here is an inversion: persist reads 'When it dies, IF IT HAD NO -1/-1 COUNTERS ON IT, return it to the battlefield with a -1/-1 counter on it', so a counter is what SPENDS a persist. This is the one blight deck in the cube that does not want counters on its own creatures, and Rhys, the Evermore and Perfect Intimidation ('Remove all counters from target creature') are what refund a spent one. Winnowing is the payoff that ties both halves together — a symmetric sacrifice sweeper that is one-sided once Isilu is out, because everything we lose to it persists straight back.

sideboard.when_to_board: vs artifacts (11 cards, 4.2%) and enchantments (21 cards, 8.1%) — 'you may blight 2 ... choose one, or BOTH if the additional cost was paid: destroy target artifact or enchantment; destroy target creature with mana value 3 or greater'. The blight is optional, which matters here: a self-inflicted counter would spend a persist

sideboard.oracle_text: Put four -1/-1 counters on target creature.
sideboard.when_to_board: vs the cube's largest measured threat class — evasion, 41 cards at 15.8% density. 'Put four -1/-1 counters on target creature' is instant-speed, kills toughness 4 or less, and costs our own board nothing

strategy_es: control de recursión con persist y blight / contadores como persists gastados
identity_es: Un control W/B que responde al tablero con ocho cartas de interacción del principal de MV 1-6 — seis de ellas eliminación barata de MV 1-3 — y que luego gana porque sus propias criaturas dejan de quedarse muertas. Se enuncia como eliminación más recursión y no como un mazo de persist, porque la manta de persist es una carta de cuarenta: Isilu, Carrier of Twilight — la cara trasera de Eirdu — otorga persist a todas las demás criaturas no-ficha, y es el techo, no el suelo. El suelo es que Reaping Willow, Dose of Dawnglow, Graveshifter y Retched Wretch recompran criaturas sin referencia alguna a Isilu. Lo que hace que la mecánica de blight importe aquí es una inversión: persist dice 'When it dies, IF IT HAD NO -1/-1 COUNTERS ON IT, return it to the battlefield with a -1/-1 counter on it', así que un contador es lo que GASTA un persist. Este es el único mazo de blight del cubo que no quiere contadores en sus propias criaturas, y Rhys, the Evermore y Perfect Intimidation ('Remove all counters from target creature') son lo que reembolsa uno gastado. Winnowing es la recompensa que ata ambas mitades: un barredor simétrico por sacrificio que es unilateral en cuanto Isilu está fuera, porque todo lo que perdemos con él vuelve de inmediato por persist.
